questions.prompt: $\_\,\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. What number goes in front of $\text{H}_2$?
questions.explanation: Four H atoms on the right need $2\text{H}_2$ on the left.

questions.prompt: $\text{N}_2 + \_\,\text{H}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3$. What number goes in front of $\text{H}_2$?
questions.explanation: $2\text{NH}_3$ has 6 H atoms, so we need $3\text{H}_2$.

questions.prompt: Balance $\text{CH}_4 + \_\,\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. What is the coefficient of $\text{O}_2$?
questions.explanation: Right side: 2 O in $\text{CO}_2$ + 2 O in $2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ = 4 O, so $2\text{O}_2$.
2 Mg and 2 O on each side. Changing MgO to MgO₂ is not allowed — that's a different substance.

questions.prompt: You may change the small subscript numbers in a formula to balance an equation.
questions.explanation: Changing a subscript changes the substance. Only change the coefficients in front.

questions.prompt: Which law explains why equations must be balanced? (the law of conservation of …)
accepted: the law of conservation of mass
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of mass: atoms are not created or destroyed in a reaction.
